newsitem.title: UK: UK says air passenger traffic to more than double.
newsitem.headline: UK says air passenger traffic to more than double.

text.p: Britain's air passenger traffic is expected to double within the next 15 years according to a new government forecast published on Thursday.

The Department of Environment, Transport and the Regions (DETR) said it expected demand for air travel to grow at around 4.5 percent a year over the 20 years between 1995 and 2015, based on its median forecast.
Its full range of forecasts predict that UK airports will be handling between 242 and 378.1 million passengers a year by 2015, compared to 129.6 million in 1995.

Growth in demand at regional airports is expected to be slightly faster than growth in the core London area airports, with the proportion of total passengers using regional airports seen growing from 37 percent in 1995 to 41 percent in 2015.
Business traffic is expected to grow faster than leisure traffic and growth in foreign resident passengers is expected to be greater than growth in UK passengers.
Long-haul travel was likely to show more rapid growth than short-haul due to an increase in traffic to and from south-east Asian countries, the report said.
